question: Why does the grounded Journal chronicle read badly, and what writing rules, selection rule and examples should the prose skill carry so a year of a life reads as a story without inventing facts?

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Nine registers for scenes, dialogue, choices and in-world documents; none for a retrospective chronicle, and no chronicle examples.

sourcesChecked.source: The owner's Journal voice ruling, cto-handoff-2230 ('Expressive narrator, recorded inner life')
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Sets what may be claimed; leaves length, selection and final wording open, and says nothing on how to make grounded sentences read well.
They print each record's own summary sentence; nothing describes people by relationship or carries a scene's subject into the retelling.

title: Why the Journal chronicle reads badly, and the writing rules to fix it
usableAnswer: Six parts, each usable alone: (1) a diagnosis confirming or correcting the lane's list; (2) a chronicle register written to drop into surface-registers.md and owner-authoring-contract.md (person, tense, introducing people, carrying a scene's subject into a retelling, joins, what a year leaves out); (3) a selection rule code can apply to any life; (4) which record fields beyond the summary sentence the Journal may draw on, such as the relationship to name a person by or the scene's premise; (5) the sample's 2026 year rewritten from its record as a target; (6) two or three approved and rejected examples in the shape of examples/approved.jsonl and rejected.jsonl.
whyItMatters: The owner reads the Journal to see his life back and has now rejected the grounded version on sight. The lane cannot fix it by adding facts, and without a register and a selection rule every further attempt will read the same way.

candidateAnswers.label: Story from turning points, context from the record
candidateAnswers.position: Each year opens on its turning points, names people by their recorded relationship, carries the scene's premise to explain what a line refers to, folds routine into at most one sentence, and drops bookkeeping.
candidateAnswers.argumentFor: Addresses every item in the diagnosis with fields the record already holds, and matches the owner's own example, which is built on turning points.
candidateAnswers.argumentAgainst: Needs a rule for what counts as a turning point, and some scene premises are written for the moment and would need their own retelling line.

candidateAnswers.label: Rewrite the scenes' result lines for retelling
candidateAnswers.position: Give every scene choice a second, retrospective result sentence authored for the Journal, and keep the chronicle's joins simple.
candidateAnswers.argumentFor: Each line then reads well on its own, authored once.
candidateAnswers.argumentAgainst: A large authoring job across every scene, and it still leaves the year unweighed.
